 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed application under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of Motorcycle bearing KA-64-U-6127, alleging that on 27.04.2022 at about 3.00 p.m.,
when riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA- 41-R-9406 on Vidhuraswath-Ramachandrapura Road, in front of Devi Bar, Gowdasandra Cross, Gowribidanur taluk, rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-U-6127 rode the same negligently from Gowdasandra village, dashed the same to the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-R- 9406, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

3. Regarding the accident on 14.12.2022 Gowribidanur police registered crime No.118/2022.
4. As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged about 20 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/- p.m. by working at Floc Chem Pharma Pvt. Ltd., Hindupuram.

5. In response to the notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective advocates,
filed written statements denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 11.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 27.04.2022 at about 3.00 p.m., on Vidhuraswatha - Ramachandrapura road, in front of Devi Bar, Gowdasandra Cross,
Gowribidanur Taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Moorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-U- 6127 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

15. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated regarding the accident after three days of the accident his father filed complaint and his father never witnessed the accident.
Petitioner submitted ignorance about identification of the person who informed about the accident to his father.
Petitioner submitted that as his father engaged in caring him, there might be delay in filing the complaint.

Petitioner stated that immediately after accident, he has been shifted to Govt. hospital, Gowribidanur.

16. In the evidence P.W.2, SDA of Govt. hospital, Gowribidanur produced copy of MLC Register extract and copy of Referral book with respect to petitioner at Ex.P.14 and 15.
17.

21. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to rebut the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

As per the Judgments cited on behalf of the petitioner, the delay caused in filing the complaint alone is insufficient to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

22. Hence, I have concluded that on 27.04.2022 at about 3.00 p.m. when petitioner was riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-R-9406 on Vidhuraswath- Ramachandrapura Road, in front of Devi Bar, Gowdasandra Cross, Gowribidanur taluk, Vasanth E., S/o.Eshwarappa negligently rode the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-U-6127 from Gowdasandra village, dashed to the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-R-9406, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident suffered ZMC fracture, left writ fracture, loss of teeth, swelling over left side of face and left eye lid and left side black eye, took treatment at Gowribidanur Govt. hospital, then took treatment at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient by spending Rs.1,00,000/- and as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.20,000/- p.m.
by working at Flow Chem Pharma Pvt. Ltd., Hindupuram.
24.
In the written statements, respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
25. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion that, he never undergone surgery.
Petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident, he neither an employee of Flow Chem Pharma Pvt. Ltd., nor earned Rs.20,000/- p.m.
26.
In the evidence P.W.2 stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of injuries suffered by the petitioner.

27. In the evidence affidavit P.W.3-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. stated that on 11.11.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner, noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent disability at 32% to left arm,
which is about 11% to whole body.

In the evidence P.W.3 produced OPD card dated 11.11.2024 and X-ray at Exs.P.16 and 17.
28.
In the cross-examination P.W.3 admitted that he never treated the petitioner.
P.W.3 stated that he has not verified inpatient treatment record of the petitioner.
P.W.3 submitted that as on 11.11.2024 fractures of the petitioner are united.

29. In the copy of Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10, date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 18.07.2003.
30.
In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding his occupation and quantum of income.
In the file, there are no evidence to show either loss of income or decrease in the income of petitioner subsequent to treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.
Hence, I have inferred that oral evidence of P.W.3-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. is insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

31. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of the petitioner, I award compensation under the following heads:
Sl
. No .
Heads of Compensation Amount (Rs.)

1) Pain and agony 50,000.00 2) Treatment charges 2,438.00 3) Conveyance, nourishment and 5,000.00 attendant charges 4) Loss of income during treatment 93,000.00 period (Rs.15,500/- x 6)
5) Loss of amenities and future 30,000.00 unhappiness:
Total: 1,80,438.00 32.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,80,438/-
with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
33. In the written statement respondent No.1 Insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Motorcycle bearing KA-64-U-6127 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.2 owner of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-U-6127 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of the Motorcycle bearing KA-64-U-6127 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:

1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 27.04.2022 at about 3.00 p.m., on Vidhuraswatha - Ramachandrapura road, in front of Devi Bar, Gowdasandra Cross,
Gowribidanur Taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Moorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-U- 6127 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner by analyzing the evidence available in the file requested to answer Issue No.1 and 2 in favour of the petitioner and award compensation as claimed in the petition by relying on the following judgments:
1. (2011) 4 Supreme Court Cases 693 (Ravi -Vs- Badrinarayan & Others),
D.D.18.02.2011.
2. 2022 ACJ 170, High Court of Karnataka at Bengaluru, MFA No.5371 & 5378/2016,
(Venkatesha K.N. -Vs- Thipregowda & Others).
11.
In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.1-Insurance Company by analyzing the evidence available on file, especially noting the delay caused in filing the complaint,
requested to answer Issue No.1 in favour of Insurance company.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
21. In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to rebut the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.
As per the Judgments cited on behalf of the petitioner, the delay caused in filing the complaint alone is insufficient to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.
In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding his occupation and quantum of income.
In the file, there are no evidence to show either loss of income or decrease in the income of petitioner subsequent to treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.
Hence, I have inferred that oral evidence of P.W.3-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. is insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.
31. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of the petitioner, I award compensation under the following heads:
Sl
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,80,438/-
with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
33. In the written statement respondent No.1 Insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the Motorcycle bearing KA-64-U-6127 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.2 owner of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-64-U-6127 has violated any terms of the policy.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of the Motorcycle bearing KA-64-U-6127 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
Govardhana C.J vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56857139/
6 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,80,438/- (Rupees One lakh eighty thousand four hundred and thirty eight only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the Motorcycle bearing KA-64-U-6127 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
